translation.english_title: The lamp that lights our household life

english_lines: The lamp that lights our household life,
Is the form of my queen of the heart.
notes: The source turn label `தங்` is kept exactly and is not expanded to an inferred character name.

english_lines: The flame that shines within this lamp,
Is the form of my brave one.
notes: The flame/lamp image is preserved rather than paraphrased into a generic declaration of love.

english_lines: The form of a young peacock.
The lamp that lights our household life,
Is the lamp of our love.
notes: The source repeats `தீபம்`; the English repeats `lamp` rather than varying the word for stylistic smoothness.

english_lines: O fruit! O sugarcane-Tamil! O nectar!
O flower where dew sleeps! O moon!
notes: `கன்னல் தமிழே` is kept as the striking `sugarcane-Tamil` image instead of being flattened to `sweet words`.
`பனி தூங்கும் மலரே` remains `flower where dew sleeps`, preserving Kalaignar's personifying image.

english_lines: With your tender speech, me myself,
You have captivated — O magnetic statue!
notes: The unusual `காந்தச் சிலையே` is retained as `magnetic statue` rather than replaced with a smoother `magnetic beauty`.
The slightly emphatic `எனையே` is allowed to remain audible in the English instead of disappearing into neutral syntax.

english_lines: When I see you, the feeling that seeps through my heart —
For those who would write that very feeling,
There are no letters at all.
notes: The source's image of feeling `seeping` into the heart and the claim that language itself lacks letters are both retained.

english_lines: Every day like this festival day, dancing and singing,
notes: The joined source form `போல்தினம்` is not used to alter the Tamil witness; the English follows the visible festival/day syntax.
`தேன் போல் வாழ்வோம்` remains the literal honey image.
The anthology prints only the abbreviated refrain cue; it is not expanded or reconstructed.

translator_notes: Exact Tamil turn labels `தங்`, `கல்`, and `தங்,கல்` remain unexpanded because the anthology itself does not spell out the identities on this lyric page.

The pilot deliberately keeps images such as `queen of the heart`, `young peacock`, `sugarcane-Tamil`, `dew sleeps`, `magnetic statue`, and `live like honey` instead of replacing them with generic romantic English.
This is a literary source-faithful translation, not a singable adaptation.
